perspective:
From Ethan Mohamud’s perspective, he knows:

- He is a plumber and Gary Guo is his close friend and a doctor; they met in middle school and have remained close.
- He noticed Gary working extremely long hours at the hospital, often skipping meals and sacrificing sleep. Concerned, Ethan invited Gary to a two-day weekend retreat for relaxation.
- Gary initially told him he appreciated the concern but could not go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- During the retreat, Ethan saw Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected something more than professional obligations was going on.
- Ethan confronted Gary, reminding him they had been friends since middle school and that he could tell him anything without judgment. Gary responded that it was complicated and he did not want to burden Ethan.
- Gary then opened up to Ethan about pressure from managing a new department and personal challenges. Ethan felt relief and empathy, and suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating some responsibilities. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary, discussed his progress and challenges, and saw Gary making efforts to change. Gary told him things were better, he was less overwhelmed, and he had had time for a movie. Ethan felt hopeful and proud and offered continued support.
- After a year, Ethan saw Gary managing on his own with a healthier balance. Ethan told Gary he was always a call away and believed Gary had it. Gary thanked him, said he could not have done it without Ethan’s support, and felt more in control. Ethan decided to step back while remaining available.
